newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - June 20.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- The director of China's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, Lu Ping, arrived in the territory to make final preparations for the handover ceremony.

-- WEN WEI PO -- With the handover approaching, Shenzehn is experiencing a new wave of investment from Hong Kong, showing that Hong Kong businessmen are confident in the prospects for Hong Kong-Shenzhen economic cooperation.

-- MING PAO -- British Prime Minister Tony Blair hoped to meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin alone during the handover ceremony. Vice-Premier Qian Qichen would arrive here earlier than previously scheduled to make arrangements for the meeting.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Governor Chris Patten said in his last Legislative Council session that his biggest regret during his five years in Hong Kong was his failure to persuade Chinese leaders to trust Hong Kong people and support political reforms.

-- A bus terminal in Stanley will have to be moved after the handover because it is located on the People's Liberation Army Hong Kong garrison's future camp. If done, more than 300 primary school pupils will have to walk to school after the handover.
-- SING TAO -- Because of disagreements over the legality of the provisional legislature, a judge decided to rush through the sentencing procedure for a case before the handover.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Sources said the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has started to investigate how local banks give credit to securities firms and clients buying and selling shares, which follows steps taken by securities regulators and the exchange to look into margin services provided by securities companies,
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- CM Telecom International announced plans to become the first Hong Kong firm to shift its primary listing from Singapore back to the territory.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- New World Development was investing HK$3 billion in Wuhan to develop housing and infrastructure projects in and around the city. The work will be a joint effort with the Wuhan city government.
